findings.title: Index on 400M-row `events` table is built without CONCURRENTLY
findings.explanation: A plain CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock on `events`. That blocks all INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on the table for the whole build, which on about 400M rows could take many minutes. Event writes would stall or time out, and requests would pile up during the deploy, and old and new app versions would both be affected during a rolling deploy. docs/CONVENTIONS.md requires CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for this table. Change the statement to `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);`.

findings.title: Missing `-- migrate:no-transaction` header
findings.explanation: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block. The migration file must start with `-- migrate:no-transaction`, as 004_events.sql does. Without it the migration fails once CONCURRENTLY is added.

findings.title: Make the migration safe to re-run after a failed concurrent build
findings.explanation: If a concurrent build fails or is cancelled, it leaves an INVALID index with the same name, and a retry then fails with 'relation already exists'. Use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS`, and note in the PR a runbook step to drop any invalid index (`DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_project_id_idx`) before retrying. Also set an appropriate lock_timeout and check that the migration runner's statement_timeout will not kill a long build.

findings.title: Consider a partial or leaner index, and check disk and write overhead
findings.explanation: `project_id` is nullable, and many events probably have no project, so `WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL` would make the index smaller. Even so, an index on 400M rows adds noticeable disk use and write amplification. Please state the expected size and confirm with EXPLAIN that the planner uses the index for `WHERE project_id = $1 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 100`. The query is already index-friendly, since it matches the index order.

Review this pull request.

## Speed up the project activity feed

The project events endpoint does a sequential scan per project. Adds an index on `events (project_id, id DESC)` to match the query.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/migrations/005_events_project_idx.sql b/migrations/005_events_project_idx.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0586576
--- /dev/null
+++ b/migrations/005_events_project_idx.sql
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+CREATE INDEX events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);
```

Before answering, check the change specifically for: authorization and tenant isolation; race conditions and concurrent requests; database migration safety on large tables and during rolling deploys; API changes that break existing clients; retries and idempotency of side effects such as payments; date and time handling; injection; sensitive data in logs; pagination and boundary conditions.
